a: The full path of the file or object.
If path is a directory, setting this to true will make it the default ACL for entities created inside the directory. Setting default causes an error if path is a file.
The actual user or group that the ACL applies to when matching entity types user or group are selected.
DEPRECATED. The ACL to set or remove. This must always be quoted in the form of <etype>:<qualifier>:<perms>. The qualifier may be empty for some types, but the type and perms are always required.
The entity type of the ACL to apply, see setfacl documentation for more info.
Whether to follow symlinks on the path if a symlink is encountered.

The permissions to apply/remove can be any combination of r, w, x (read, write and execute respectively), and X (execute permission if the file is a directory or already has execute permission for some user)
Select if and when to recalculate the effective right masks of the files. See setfacl documentation for more info. Incompatible with state.
Recursively sets the specified ACL. Incompatible with state. Alias recurse added in version 1.3.0.
Define whether the ACL should be present or not. The query state gets the current ACL without changing it, for use in register operations.

Use NFSv4 ACLs instead of POSIX ACLs. This feature uses nfs4_setfacl and nfs4_getfacl. The behavior depends on those implementation. And currently it only supports A in ACE, so D must be replaced with the appropriate A.
ansible.posix.acl.d: Set and retrieve file ACL information.

a: A command to be executed in the future.
The count of units in the future to execute the command or script file.
An existing script file to be executed in the future.
The state dictates if the command or script file should be evaluated as present (added) or absent (deleted).
If a matching job is present a new job will not be added.
The type of units in the future to execute the command or script file.
ansible.posix.at.d: Schedule the execution of a command or script file via the at command

a: The SSH public key(s), as a string or (since Ansible 1.9) url (https://github.com/username.keys). You can also use file:// prefix to search remote for a file with SSH key(s).
The username on the remote host whose authorized_keys file will be modified.
Change the comment on the public key. Rewriting the comment is useful in cases such as fetching it from GitHub or GitLab. If no comment is specified, the existing comment will be kept.
Whether to remove all other non-specified keys from the authorized_keys file. Multiple keys can be specified in a single key string value by separating them by newlines.
Follow path symlink instead of replacing it.
A string of ssh key options to be prepended to the key in the authorized_keys file.
Whether this module should manage the directory of the authorized key file. If set to true, the module will create the directory, as well as set the owner and permissions of an existing directory.

Alternative path to the authorized_keys file. The default value is the .ssh/authorized_keys of the home of the user specified in the user parameter. Most of the time, it is not necessary to set this key.
Whether the given key (with the given key_options) should or should not be in the file.
This only applies if using a https url as the source of the keys. If set to false, the SSL certificates will not be validated.
ansible.posix.authorized_key.d: Adds or removes an SSH authorized key

a: Enable or disable a setting. For ports: Should this port accept (enabled) or reject (disabled) connections. The states present and absent can only be used in zone level operations (i.e.
The forward setting you would like to enable/disable to/from zones within firewalld. This option only is supported by firewalld v0.9.0 or later.
The ICMP block you would like to add/remove to/from a zone in firewalld.
Enable/Disable inversion of ICMP blocks for a zone in firewalld. Note that the option type is changed to bool in ansible.posix version 2.0.0 and later.
Whether to apply this change to the runtime firewalld configuration. Defaults to true if permanent.
The interface you would like to add/remove to/from a zone in firewalld.
The masquerade setting you would like to enable/disable to/from zones within firewalld. Note that the option type is changed to bool in ansible.posix version 2.0.0 and later.
Ignores immediate if permanent and firewalld is not running.
Whether to apply this change to the permanent firewalld configuration. As of Ansible 2.3, permanent operations can operate on firewalld configs when it is not running (requires firewalld >= 0.3.9).
Name of a port or port range to add/remove to/from firewalld. Must be in the form PORT/PROTOCOL or PORT-PORT/PROTOCOL for port ranges.
Name of a protocol to add/remove to/from firewalld.
Rich rule to add/remove to/from firewalld. See Syntax for firewalld rich language rules.
Name of a service to add/remove to/from firewalld. The service must be listed in output of firewall-cmd --get-services.
The source/network you would like to add/remove to/from firewalld.
firewalld Zone target. If state, this will reset the target to default.
The amount of time in seconds the rule should be in effect for when non-permanent.
The firewalld zone to add/remove to/from. Note that the default zone can be configured per system but public is default from upstream.
Gather information about specific zones. If only works if active_zones.
Path to the mount point (e.g. /mnt/files). Before Ansible 2.3 this option was only usable as ignore:dest, ignore:destfile, and name.
If mounted, the device will be actively mounted and appropriately configured in fstab. If the mount point is not present, the mount point will be created.
Create a backup file including the timestamp information so you can get the original file back if you somehow clobbered it incorrectly.
Determines if the filesystem should be mounted on boot. Only applies to Solaris and Linux systems. For Solaris systems, true will set yes as the value of mount at boot in /etc/vfstab.
Dump (see fstab(5)). Note that if set to null and state, it will cease to work and duplicate entries will be made with subsequent runs. Has no effect on Solaris systems or when used with state.
File to use instead of /etc/fstab. You should not use this option unless you really know what you are doing. This might be useful if you need to configure mountpoints in a chroot environment.
Filesystem type. Required when state is present, mounted, or ephemeral.
Mount options (see fstab(5), or vfstab(4) on Solaris).

Passno (see fstab(5)). Note that if set to null and state, it will cease to work and duplicate entries will be made with subsequent runs. Deprecated on Solaris systems. Has no effect when used with state.
Device (or NFS volume, or something else) to be mounted on path. Required when state set to present, mounted, or ephemeral. Ignored when state set to absent or unmounted.
ansible.posix.mount.d: Control active and configured mount points

a: Path of the patch file as accepted by the GNU patch tool. If remote_src, the patch source file is looked up from the module's files directory.
Passes --backup --version-control to patch, producing numbered backup copies.
Path of a base directory in which the patch file will be applied. May be omitted when dest option is specified, otherwise required.
Setting to true will disable patch's heuristic for transforming CRLF line endings into LF. Line endings of src and dest must match. If set to false, patch will replace CRLF in src files on POSIX.

Path of the file on the remote machine to be patched. The names of the files to be patched are usually taken from the patch file, but if there's just one file to be patched it can specified with this option.
Setting to true will ignore white space changes between patch and input.
If false, it will search for src at originating/controller machine, If true, it will go to the remote/target machine for the src.
Whether the patch should be applied or reverted.

Number that indicates the smallest prefix containing leading slashes that will be stripped from each file name found in the patch file. For more information see the strip parameter of the GNU patch tool.
ansible.posix.patch.d: Apply patch files using the GNU patch tool

ansible.posix.rhel_facts.d: Facts module to set or override RHEL specific facts.

a: A package name or package specifier with version, like name-1.0. Comparison operators for package version are valid here >, <, >, <. Example - name>.
Whether to install (present or installed, latest), or remove (absent or removed) a package. present and installed will simply ensure that a desired package is installed.
ansible.posix.rhel_rpm_ostree.d: Ensure packages exist in a RHEL for Edge rpm-ostree based system

a: Allow for the upgrade to be a chronologically older tree.
Perform the transaction using only pre-cached data, do not download.
The OSNAME upon which to operate.
Force peer-to-peer connection instead of using a system message bus.
Name of the boolean to configure.
Useful for scenarios (chrooted environment) that you can't get the real SELinux state.
Set to true if the boolean setting should survive a reboot.
The path to the SELinux configuration file, if non-standard.
The name of the SELinux policy to use (e.g. targeted) will be required unless state.
If set to true, will update also the kernel boot parameters when disabling/enabling SELinux. The grubby tool must be present on the target system for this to work.
ansible.posix.selinux.d: Change policy and state of SELinux

a: Path on the destination host that will be synchronized from the source. The path can be absolute or relative.
Path on the source host that will be synchronized to the destination. The path can be absolute or relative.
Internal use only. See use_ssh_args for ssh arg settings.
Mirrors the rsync archive flag, enables recursive, links, perms, times, owner, group flags, and -D.
Skip based on checksum, rather than mod-time & size; Note that that archive option is still enabled by default - the checksum option will not disable it.
Compress file data during the transfer. In most cases, leave this enabled unless it causes problems.
Copy symlinks as the item that they point to (the referent) is copied, rather than the symlink.
This option puts the temporary file from each updated file into a holding directory until the end of the transfer, at which time all the files are renamed into place in rapid succession.
Delete files in dest that do not exist (after transfer, not before) in the src path. This option requires recursive. This option ignores excluded files and behaves like the rsync opt --delete-after.
Port number for ssh on the destination host. Prior to Ansible 2.0, the ansible_ssh_port inventory var took precedence over this value.
Skip creating new files on receiver.
Preserve group. This parameter defaults to the value of the archive option.
Add a destination to hard link against during the rsync.
Copy symlinks as symlinks. This parameter defaults to the value of the archive option.
Specify the direction of the synchronization. In push mode the localhost or delegate is the source. In pull mode the remote host in context is the source.
Preserve owner (super user only). This parameter defaults to the value of the archive option.
Tells rsync to keep the partial file which should make a subsequent transfer of the rest of the file much faster.
Preserve permissions. This parameter defaults to the value of the archive option.
Specify the private key to use for SSH-based rsync connections (e.g. ~/.ssh/id_rsa).
Recurse into directories. This parameter defaults to the value of the archive option.
Specify additional rsync options by passing in an array. Note that an empty string in rsync_opts will end up transfer the current working directory.

Specify the rsync command to run on the remote host. See --rsync-path on the rsync man page. To specify the rsync command to run on the local host, you need to set this your task var ansible_rsync_path.
Specify a --timeout for the rsync command in seconds.
Put user@ for the remote paths. If you have a custom ssh config to define the remote user for a host that does not match the inventory user, you should set this parameter to false.

SSH connection multiplexing for rsync is disabled by default to prevent misconfigured ControlSockets from resulting in failed SSH connections. This is accomplished by setting the SSH ControlSocket to none.
Preserve modification times. This parameter defaults to the value of the archive option.

In Ansible 2.10 and lower, it uses the ssh_args specified in ansible.cfg. In Ansible 2.11 and onwards, when set to true, it uses all SSH connection configurations like ansible_ssh_args, ansible_ssh_common_args, and…
ansible.posix.synchronize.d: A wrapper around rsync to make common tasks in your playbooks quick and easy

a: The dot-separated path (also known as key) specifying the sysctl variable.
Use this option to ignore errors about unknown keys.
If true, performs a /sbin/sysctl -p if the sysctl_file is updated. If false, does not reload sysctl even if the sysctl_file is updated.
Whether the entry should be present or absent in the sysctl file.
Specifies the absolute path to sysctl.conf, if not /etc/sysctl.conf.
Verify token value with the sysctl command and set with -w if necessary.
Desired value of the sysctl key.
